text:
Predicates:
GoodGuys(x) ::: x are the good guys.
Win(x, y) ::: x wins y.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
NameAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
Character(x) ::: x is a character.
Movie(x) ::: x is a movie.
FightsNemesis(x, y) ::: x fights y and y is the nemesis of x.
InMovie(x, y) ::: x is in y.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
InMovie(x, y) ::: x is in y.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: x is the nemesis of y.
SurprisingAdventures ::: the movie "The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar."
SirDigby ::: the character Sir Digby.
Premises:
∀x (GoodGuys(x) → Wins(x, y)) ::: Good guys always win.
SurprisingAdventures is a movie.
FightsNemesis(SirDigby, y) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
NameAfter(SurprisingAdventures, SirDigby) ::: The movie "The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar" is named after Sir Digby.
NamedAfter(SurprisingAdventures, SirDigby) ::: The movie is named after Sir Digby.
InMovie(SirDigby, SurprisingAdventures) ::: Sir Digby is in the movie.
InMovie(y, SurprisingAdventures) ::: y (the nemesis) is in the movie.
If x fights y and y is the nemesis of x, then y does not win.
∀x ∀y (FightsNemesis(x, y) → ¬Win(y, x)) ::: If someone fights their nemesis, the nemesis does not win.
